title: ci-cd-rollback-breadcrumbs-notes-10
content:
Breadcrumbs / scratchpad for the canary rollback (notes to self)

Summary:
- Canary deploy of release v2025-02-18 (api-server + serving-runtime changes) started 2025-02-18 22:15 UTC.
- By ~22:40 UTC ~8/10 canary requests started returning 504 / high latency (95p token latency spiked from ~120ms -> >2.5s). Error rate ~12% vs baseline <0.5%.
- Decided to abort canary and roll back to previous stable image (v2025-02-11). This doc contains commands I ran, error snippets, quick hypotheses, and follow-up tasks.

Raw commands and outputs (copied from terminals):
- Check rollout status (k8s canary deployment):
  $ kubectl -n prod get deploy api-server-canary -o wide
  NAME                 READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
  api-server-canary    3/5     5            3           25m

  $ kubectl -n prod describe deploy api-server-canary
  Events:
    Type    Reason             Age   From                   Message
    ----    ------             ----  ----                   -------
    Warning UnhealthyPod       5m    kubelet, ip-10-0-0-5    Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 504

- Inspect pod logs for one failing canary pod:
  $ kubectl -n prod logs api-server-canary-5f7b8c9d-zz4p -c api-server --since=30m
  2025-02-18T22:36:02Z ERROR request_handler.go:412 requestID=aa3f420a status=504 upstream=serving-runtime timed out waiting for response after 10s
  2025-02-18T22:36:05Z WARN serving_client.go:78 fallback triggered: model-serving timeout

- Check serving-runtime / model pods around same time:
  $ kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide
  NAME                                     READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
  serving-runtime-0                        1/1     Running   0          3d
  serving-runtime-1                        0/1     CrashLoopBackOff 6   30m

  $ kubectl -n prod logs serving-runtime-1 -c runtime --tail=200
  2025-02-18T22:35:40Z ERROR runtime_worker.go:210 OOMKilled: attempted to allocate 1.6GB (available 1.2GB)
  2025-02-18T22:35:41Z INFO healthcheck.go:56 health check failed: memory usage 78% > threshold 75%

- Canary rollback executed (manual):
  $ helm -n prod history redwood-api-server
  REVISION    UPDATED                     STATUS      CHART               APP VERSION
  21          2025-02-11T13:10:02Z       deployed    api-server-1.4.2     v2025-02-11-7f8e9d0
  22          2025-02-18T22:15:02Z       deployed    api-server-1.5.0     v2025-02-18-1a2b3c4

  $ helm -n prod rollback redwood-api-server 21
  Rollback to 21 initiated
  $ kubectl -n prod rollout status deploy/api-server
  deployment "api-server" successfully rolled out

- Post-rollback verification:
  - Canary error rate dropped back to baseline within ~6 minutes.
  - Graphs (Datadog): 95p latency returned to ~130ms; error rate <0.5%.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Memory regression in 1.5.0 build caused OOMs under canary load (most likely). Evidence: runtime pod OOMKilled, memory healthcheck tripped. Also new quantization change in model loader in 1.5.0 (PR #1789) increases peak memory for certain batch sizes.
2) Autoscaler misconfig / pod resource requests were too low for new runtime binary (secondary). Canary had same resource requests as stable. Metrics show higher RSS for runtime under identical load.
3) New kernel selection path (GPU kernel tweak) had edge-case that causes slowdowns and timeouts when sequence length > 1024. Less likely because errors show OOM rather than slow compute.
4) Upstream model checkpoint change (not in this release) — unlikely, but note to verify model image tags.

What I tried and immediate outcomes:
- Increased serving-runtime memory limit on canary >= 2.5GB -> pod stabilized locally but still saw occasional 504s (suggests memory is part of problem but not the only factor).
- Replayed failing requests against canary in staging with stress tool (same token-length distribution) -> reproduced memory spike -> OOM on default limits.
- Manually re-deployed canary without the quantization change (build with flag QUANTIZE=false) -> no OOMs in short run.
- Rolled back production canary to stable (helm rollback) -> production error rate fixed.

Immediate follow-ups (short term):
- ACTION: Pin prod canary image to v2025-02-11 for now and block 1.5.0 rollout until root cause determined (PR hold). Owner: @Samira.
- ACTION: Open a regression ticket linking PR #1789, INC-5421, and this notes doc. Owner: @Jordan.
- ACTION: Run a targeted mem/latency profile on 1.5.0 runtime with batch sizes [1,4,8,16] and seq lengths [256,512,1024,2048]. Owner: @Liam.
- ACTION: Increase default serving-runtime pod requests/limits for canary to be conservative (temp). Owner: @Priya.
- ACTION: Add additional canary readiness probe checks that include a simple model inference micro-benchmark (to catch slow kernels). Owner: @Release-Eng.

Longer term / investigation notes:
- Suspect the quantization loader change increases peak per-request memory due to prefetch buffer + cache alignment. Need flame graphs.
- Check build artifact: api-server:v2025-02-18-1a2b3c4 includes runtime v0.9.7 and model-loader v2.3.4. Compare with stable runtime v0.9.5 + model-loader v2.2.1.
- Re-run CI performance tests with the exact canary image under scaled traffic (50 rps) and capture GPU/CPU RSS and GC metrics.
- Consider canary traffic shaping: start with 1% -> 5% -> 10% with memory/latency checks between steps. Our current canary was 10% immediate which made regression visible faster but riskier.

Notes / questions for follow-up sync (tomorrow):
- Did we change default JVM/Go memory flags in the runtime build? (I think PR #1789 touches native allocator flags)
- Are there known interactions between the quantization prefetch and pinned GPU memory that could cause host OOM?
- Should we add a pre-deploy smoke that runs the small-batch model inference to the CI pipeline for each runtime build?

Links / artifacts to attach to the regression ticket:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1789
- Canary logs (Datadog dashboards): link -> Inc dashboard (INC-5421)
- Helm diff for 1.5.0 vs 1.4.2 (saved locally: /home/jordan/helm-diffs/1.5.0-vs-1.4.2.diff)
- Slack incident thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234567/p1700200000000000

Quick TL;DR to paste into incident report:
- Canary of v2025-02-18 caused elevated 504s and OOMs in serving-runtime; rolled back to v2025-02-11. Immediate mitigation: rollback and increase canary memory limits. Root cause suspect: memory regression from quantization change in PR #1789.

This doc is intentionally messy — breadcrumbs for the future. If anyone picks this up:
- start with the memory profile comparisons, then verify whether quantize flag toggles behavior, then check autoscaler/resource defaults.

-- Jordan
